title: Draft systems
lead: What happens between the keg and the faucet, and the parts you can look after.

sections.name: Keg to faucet

lines.label: In short
lines.text: Gas pushes beer from the keg, through the lines, to the faucet.

know: Keg, coupler, lines, faucet, gas and regulator.

sections.name: Clean lines

video.title: 10 Key Elements of a Draft Beer System

keyPoints.line: pushes the beer; it doesn’t pump.

read.where: A draft system is a **keg**, a **coupler**, **beer lines**, a **faucet**, a **gas** source and **regulators**. The coupler locks onto the keg: **gas goes in** and **beer comes out**. The gas pushes beer up the keg’s spear, along the lines and out the faucet. A **regulator** controls the pressure, and the gas must be **beverage grade**: CO2, or a CO2 and nitrogen blend for some systems.

stops.name: Lines
stops.text: Carry beer to the bar, kept **cold**.

read.mixup: The gas isn’t just carbonation. It’s what moves the beer.

read.where: Cicerone’s standard is **38°F** for the cooler and the system. The Brewers Association says every keg should be **at or below 38°F** when it’s served; even a few degrees warmer causes **foaming**. A keg fresh off the truck should sit in the cooler **at least 24 hours** before it’s tapped.
read.mixup: Foaming isn’t usually the gas. Check the temperature, the coupler, a kinked hose, then call the draft pro.

video.title: How Often Should You Clean Your Draft Beer Lines?

keyPoints.line: an acid clean for beer stone.

read.bigIdea: Clean lines or the beer goes bad.
read.where: The Brewers Association says draft lines are cleaned **at least every 14 days**, with **faucets** taken apart and **couplers** scrubbed on the same schedule, and an **acid clean every three months**. Skipped cleanings grow bacteria: the most common sign is a **buttery** flavor (diacetyl); others are **sour milk** and **vinegar**. Never pour while lines are being cleaned: the chemicals are hazardous.
read.mixup: A buttery beer on draft is usually the **lines**, not the brewery.
read.sayIt: Let me pour you a fresh one and have our lines checked.

sections.name: What you do, and don’t touch

keyPoints.line: hands off: a trained person sets it.
never push a keg with compressed air.
faucets and drip trays at close.

read.bigIdea: Know your part of the system.
read.where: Gas pressure is set by a **draft-trained** person only: don’t turn the regulator to fix a pour. Never pressurize a keg with **compressed air** (a hand party pump pushes air in and the beer won’t last a day). Your part: **pour well**, keep the **faucet out of the beer**, and at close **rinse faucets and drip trays** with fresh water and let them air dry.
read.mixup: Turning the gas up doesn’t fix a foamy pour. It usually makes it worse.

sources: Brewers Association, Draught Beer Quality Manual, 4th ed., 2019 (brewersassociation.org); Cicerone, US Certified Beer Server Syllabus v6.0, 2024 (cicerone.org). Checked Nov 8, 2026.
